aspectTitle: F95 — author hover content is not itself hoverable (pop-up vanishes on the cursor path from trigger to content)
aspectDescription: The single normative failure technique for 1.4.13 (F95) describes author-built additional content that appears on pointer hover but DISAPPEARS the moment the user moves the pointer off the trigger toward the content to read it — because visibility is bound only to mouseover/mouseout on the trigger, there is a physical gap between trigger and pop-up, or there is no shared hover region. Judging this is a SPATIAL + BEHAVIORAL call: a reviewer mentally traces the cursor path and asks whether the pop-up is reachable without the mouseout firing. A static checker sees a span[role=tooltip] that toggle
scenario: SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.
mechanism: Hoverable (F95) pure dead-zone: trigger-to-popup geometry is a transparent gap (top:50px on a 20px trigger with a 30px spacer), not adjacency/overlap, and the popup carries no mouseenter, so the trigger's mouseout fires on the travel path and hides the tooltip; no continuous pointer path keeps the content visible.

scenario: Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

scenario: Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

There is no continuous pointer path despite perfect visual adjacency.

scenario: Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. aspectTitle: Applicability gate — author-controlled tooltip vs. user-agent title= tooltip (and modal-dialog carve-out)
aspectDescription: The SC explicitly does NOT apply when the additional content's appearance is 'completely controlled by the user agent' — canonically the browser rendering of the title attribute — and modal dialogs are also out of scope. F95 bakes the UA carve-out into its test (condition #2: 'controlled by the user agent, not the author'). The judgment-heavy case is attributing WHO controls the appearance: distinguishing (a) a plain title= tooltip (out of scope, passes by exclusion) from (b) an AUTHOR-built div styled/scripted to LOOK native (in scope, must meet all three conditions) and (c) the inverse where
scenario: Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.
mechanism: The hover bubble is the browser's native rendering of the title attribute. SC 1.4.13 explicitly excludes content whose appearance is completely controlled by the user agent (canonically the title tooltip), and F95 condition #2 ('controlled by the user agent, not the author') is satisfied — so the failure does not apply. Verified with Puppeteer: 0 script tags, 0 inline on* handlers, Save title='Save your work', no author bubble element in the DOM.
